system.name: SceneX
system.one_liner: Framework that turns text descriptions into large-scale 3D scenes by having an LLM planner drive procedural modules and assets in Blender.

content.variant_note: four slanted render strips as a teaser, then two titled component boxes (planner and hub) and a strip of user instructions
content.argues: One system can build both natural scenes and unbounded cities from short text instructions, by combining a planner with a hub of procedural modules and assets.
content.subject: Rendered scene strips above the PCGPlanner stage chain and the PCGHub module list, with the user instructions below.

lessons.what_to_learn: Open with a full-width band of the system's own renders cut into slanted strips, then give each component its own titled box below; a bottom strip with the user instructions in the same left-to-right order as the renders links input to output without arrows.
lessons.suits: generative systems whose results are visually rich and whose method has two or three parts, such as a planner and a resource library.

evidence: The proposed SceneX can create large-scale 3D natural scenes or unbounded cities automatically according to user instructions.
we develop the PCGPlanner to coordinate PCG methods within these constraints.
PCGHub offers a platform for continuously incorporating new PCG capabilities

summary: SceneX turns short text instructions into large-scale 3D scenes, natural landscapes and unbounded cities, by combining a planner with a hub of procedural assets that run in Blender. The figure works as a teaser: four slanted strips of rendered scenes (a cherry-blossom river, a modern city, a fall forest, noonday woods) run across the top, edge to edge. Below, two dashed boxes carry the components. PCGPlanner draws a four-step staircase, Scene Decomposition, Terrain Generation, Objects Generation and Retrieval, Assets Placement, next to an LLM, API and Blender icon chain; PCGHub lists its features and counts, with a word cloud of module categories and a row of tool logos. A grey strip with the four user instructions closes the figure.

notes: Prior kinds kept in the same order (contribution-mosaic, stage-pipeline, scope-overview). The meaning of the tall grey up arrow and of the dotted down arrow labelled Scene Generate is not stated. Tool badge names are read by eye and partly legible. The digest reports no strokes because dashed outlines are filled dash segments. The render strips are the system's own outputs, so they are listed as own, not generated.
